message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you set as the target). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a reverse card is played). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card from your hand that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have only one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The round ends when a player discards all of their cards. That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round’s points to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score. | **Key Tips** 1. Keep track of the current color and number so you can anticipate what cards opponents might play. 2. Use Wild cards strategically to change the color to one you have many of. 3. Remember the penalty for playing a Wild Draw Four incorrectly—if challenged and found wrong, you must draw four cards instead of the challenger. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the scoring or add house rules for extra fun.
